code_fixes.anomaly: Fire spreads unchecked and the structure is destroyed

conclusion.root_cause: Probably a balance problem in the fire numbers, not a missing code path, though I could not fully prove it. Each burning part heats every neighbour within 8 studs by 5 heat/s, and a neighbour ignites at 40 heat. With several neighbours per part, a part burns 45s and ignites many others, which fits 3 ignitions turning into 23 spreads, 23 charred parts and a structure collapse. A burning part also gains 6 heat/s up to 100, and each litre only removes 9 heat (CoolPerLitre). Putting out a fully grown fire (heat 100 down to 10) takes about 10 litres on the same part, so a player barely outpaces the spread and no fire is ever extinguished. My server probes could not test this. FireService:Ignite returned false for all 203 sampled Flammable parts and ApplyWater returned 0 on parts that were not burning. That suggests the City parts are not indexed as a fire location in the test playtest, which is a testing artefact. The cooling and spread numbers in FireConfig are therefore the best explanation, not a proven cause.
conclusion.evidence: FireConfig: SpreadHeatPerSecond=5, IgniteAt=40, GrowPerSecond=6, CoolPerLitre=9, ExtinguishAt=10, DefaultFuel=45, SpreadRadius=8. FireSim.step heats every idle neighbour of every burning cell each tick, and FireSim.cool only subtracts CoolPerLitre*litres. Probes 6 and 7: Ignite returned false for all 203 sampled Flammable parts (8088 tagged) and ApplyWater returned 0, so the test environment could not exercise extinguishing at all. Telemetry showed fires_ignited 3, fires_spread 23 and no fires_extinguished.
conclusion.fix_hint: Retune FireConfig so fire can be fought. Lower SpreadHeatPerSecond (for example to 2) and GrowPerSecond, and raise CoolPerLitre (for example to 20-25). Also make sure the City location is indexed in FireService (MapService.LocationBuilt or InstanceBuilt) so Ignite and ApplyWater work on its Flammable parts.

--!strict
-- FireSim [owner: G1]. Pure fire maths for FireService: no Roblox APIs, so game/tests/fire_sim.spec.luau
-- runs it under the plain `luau` CLI. FireService owns the Roblox side (tags, attributes, signals).
--
--   FireSim.buildNeighbors(positions: { Pos }, radius: number): { { number } }   -- spatial hash, O(n)
--   FireSim.step(burning: { [Cell]: true }, dt: number, p: Params): ({ Edge }, { Cell })
--       burns fuel, heats idle neighbours, grows heat. Returns (ignitions, charred). It never changes
--       `state` and never adds to `burning`: the caller applies both after the loop.
--   FireSim.cool(cell: Cell, litres: number, p: Params): boolean   -- true = the fire is out now
--   FireSim.levelFor(state: number, heat: number): number          -- 0 (not burning) or 1..3
--   FireSim.inCone(dx, dy, dz, ax, ay, az, range, cosMin): boolean -- is offset d inside the spray cone
--   FireSim.canIgnite(locCount, locCap, total, globalCap): boolean -- per-instance + global fire budget
--
-- A Cell may carry extra fields (FireService adds part, level, location, cause); FireSim only touches
-- heat, fuel, state and neighbors.

local FireSim = {}

FireSim.IDLE = 0
FireSim.BURNING = 1
FireSim.CHARRED = 2

export type Pos = { x: number, y: number, z: number }
export type Cell = { heat: number, fuel: number, state: number, neighbors: { Cell } }
export type Edge = { from: Cell, to: Cell }
export type Params = {
	SpreadRadius: number,
	SpreadHeatPerSecond: number,
	GrowPerSecond: number,
	IgniteAt: number,
	ExtinguishAt: number,
	CoolPerLitre: number,
}

local function bucket(v: number, size: number): number
	return math.floor(v / size)
end

function FireSim.buildNeighbors(positions: { Pos }, radius: number): { { number } }
	local grid: { [string]: { number } } = {}
	for i, p in positions do
		local key = `{bucket(p.x, radius)},{bucket(p.y, radius)},{bucket(p.z, radius)}`
		local list = grid[key]
		if not list then
			list = {}
			grid[key] = list
		end
		table.insert(list, i)
	end
	local r2 = radius * radius
	local out: { { number } } = {}
	for i, p in positions do
		local mine: { number } = {}
		local bx, by, bz = bucket(p.x, radius), bucket(p.y, radius), bucket(p.z, radius)
		for dx = -1, 1 do
			for dy = -1, 1 do
				for dz = -1, 1 do
					for _, j in grid[`{bx + dx},{by + dy},{bz + dz}`] or {} do
						if j ~= i then
							local q = positions[j]
							local ex, ey, ez = q.x - p.x, q.y - p.y, q.z - p.z
							if ex * ex + ey * ey + ez * ez <= r2 then
								table.insert(mine, j)
							end
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end
		out[i] = mine
	end
	return out
end

function FireSim.levelFor(state: number, heat: number): number
	if state ~= FireSim.BURNING then
		return 0
	elseif heat > 80 then
		return 3
	elseif heat > 50 then
		return 2
	end
	return 1
end

function FireSim.step(burning: { [Cell]: true }, dt: number, p: Params): ({ Edge }, { Cell })
	local lit: { Edge } = {}
	local charred: { Cell } = {}
	local seen: { [Cell]: true } = {}
	for c in burning do
		c.fuel -= dt
		if c.fuel <= 0 then
			table.insert(charred, c)
			continue
		end
		for _, n in c.neighbors do
			if n.state == FireSim.IDLE then
				n.heat += p.SpreadHeatPerSecond * dt
				if n.heat >= p.IgniteAt and not seen[n] then
					seen[n] = true
					table.insert(lit, { from = c, to = n })
				end
			end
		end
		c.heat = math.min(100, c.heat + p.GrowPerSecond * dt)
	end
	return lit, charred
end

function FireSim.cool(cell: Cell, litres: number, p: Params): boolean
	cell.heat -= p.CoolPerLitre * litres
	return cell.heat <= p.ExtinguishAt
end

function FireSim.inCone(dx: number, dy: number, dz: number, ax: number, ay: number, az: number, range: number, cosMin: number): boolean
	local m = math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)
	if m > range then
		return false
	end
	if m < 1e-3 then
		return true
	end
	local am = math.sqrt(ax * ax + ay * ay + az * az)
	if am < 1e-6 then
		return false
	end
	return (dx * ax + dy * ay + dz * az) / (m * am) >= cosMin
end

-- Fire budget: every location (mission instance) has its own cap, so one runaway fire in a parallel
-- mission can't use up the server-wide cap and freeze spread in everyone else's. The global cap is a
-- last-resort safety net above the sum of normal per-instance usage.
function FireSim.canIgnite(locCount: number, locCap: number, total: number, globalCap: number): boolean
	return locCount < locCap and total < globalCap
end

return FireSim

--!strict
-- ForgeTelemetry: tiny counter API for generated games. ForgeProbe reports these counters.
--
--   local ForgeTelemetry = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").ForgeTelemetry)
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("coins_collected")      -- +1
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("damage_dealt", 25)     -- +25
--   ForgeTelemetry.get()                          -- { coins_collected = 1, damage_dealt = 25 }
--
-- Counters live as number attributes on ServerStorage.ForgeCounters (a Folder), so every VM in the
-- server (game scripts, ForgeProbe, execute_luau) sees the same values. Server only: on the client
-- count() is a no-op and get() returns {}.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local FOLDER_NAME = "ForgeCounters"

local ForgeTelemetry = {}

local function folder(): Instance?
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return nil
	end
	local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
	local f = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		f = Instance.new("Folder")
		f.Name = FOLDER_NAME
		f.Parent = ServerStorage
	end
	return f
end

-- Attribute names: letters, digits and underscores, max 100 chars, may not start with "RBX".
local function key(name: string): string
	local k = string.gsub(tostring(name), "[^%w_]", "_")
	if k == "" then
		k = "_"
	end
	if string.sub(k, 1, 3) == "RBX" then
		k = "_" .. k
	end
	return string.sub(k, 1, 100)
end

function ForgeTelemetry.count(name: string, n: number?)
	local f = folder()
	if not f then
		return
	end
	local ok = pcall(function()
		local k = key(name)
		local cur = f:GetAttribute(k)
		local add = tonumber(n) or 1
		f:SetAttribute(k, (if type(cur) == "number" then cur else 0) + add)
	end)
	if not ok then
		-- telemetry must never break the game
		return
	end
end

function ForgeTelemetry.get(): { [string]: number }
	local out: { [string]: number } = {}
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return out
	end
	local f = game:GetService("ServerStorage"):FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		return out
	end
	for k, v in f:GetAttributes() do
		if type(v) == "number" then
			out[k] = v
		end
	end
	return out
end

return ForgeTelemetry

	local n = 1
